To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mood and involvement influence impulsivity and that the decision-making stage in online shopping is divided into two stages.

(1) incidental moods tend increase process impulsivity in e-commerce; (2) this effect may not restrained by involvement; (3) decision-making process can separated into two stages: orientation and evaluation; (4) differences in impulsivity is most evident in the latter stage.
mood-elicited process impulsivity can affect consumer decisions and that this effect may not depend on involvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of mood-elicitation on consumer decision-making process and how involvement can restrain the effect.
the process of decision-making in the context of online shopping, and the influence of mood and involvement on the process.
how impulsivity affects consumer online decision-making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the process impulsivity in online purchase decisions is influenced by incidental moods and the level of product involvement, but the effects of incidental moods are more evident in the evaluation process.
mood and involvement influence the decision-making process of consumers, and that the influence of mood on the decision-making process is stronger than the influence of involvement.
the effect of mood on impulsivity in e-commerce can be moderated by involvement, but only in the orientation phase of the decision-making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mood-elicited impulsive consumer decision-making process is a complex phenomenon.
the effect of mood on consumer decision-making in the online shopping context is more profound than previously thought.
mood-elicited impulse is a key factor in online purchase behavior and it is important to understand its underlying mechanisms in order to improve the effectiveness of online marketing strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumers should be aware of the influence of their mood on their decision-making processes.
mood can affect impulsivity, and that the effect is most evident in the decision-making evaluation stage.
the process view of impulsiveness is useful in studying online shopping behavior, and that the process view may help to better understand the role of mood in online shopping decisions.
